canonical.title: Count the Number of Undirected Graphs on N Vertices
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/1. Learning/01. Count the number of graphs.cpp

narrative.title: The Network Blueprint Census
narrative.scenario: A network architect is asked how many distinct wiring plans exist for a closed lab of n machines, where every unordered machine pair may either have a cable or not — nothing else distinguishes one plan from another. Every pair contributes an independent yes/no choice, so the plans multiply out to a simple power of two.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n — the number of vertices.
narrative.outputFormat: Return 2 raised to the number of possible undirected edges, i.e. 2^(n*(n-1)/2).

testCases.explanation: A lone vertex has no possible edges, so only the empty graph exists.
Three vertex pairs means 2^3 = 8 wiring plans.

hintLevels: Level 1: Count how many unordered vertex pairs could carry a wire.
Level 2: n choose 2 pairs exist; each pair is an independent present-or-absent decision.
Level 3: The answer is 2^(n(n-1)/2) — no enumeration is ever needed.
